findings.body: Raise: Not done. Native routing is decided only for the initial Claude choice here. When a user-facing `split` round runs through the Claude SDK from a Codex session and Claude fails, the fallback at worker.py:245-300 switches to Codex but calls `codex.run` instead of handing out a `frontend` subagent. It can also refuse for a missing Codex SDK after the status commit, although a native Codex round needs no SDK. The named rule that work on the coordinating session's tool runs as its background subagent is unmet for this fallback.
findings.title: Not done: split fallback uses the Codex kit inside a Codex session

findings.body: Raise: Functional. New evidence beyond the earlier ruling about an expired session: every native fix handout returns here, but the next `forge land` starts `rounds` from zero at land.py:35. No round count is saved across hand-back. If close alternates between new review findings and failing checks, so its repeated-failure guard does not stop the item, each rerun prints `Fix round 1 of 3` and the three-round land limit is never reached. The existing land test covers that alternating sequence only within one kit-run invocation; the native test covers one fix round.
findings.title: Native land handouts reset the three-round fix limit

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: a third angle on land and handed-out rounds; when the session exits before handback, a land rerun closes only the committed work, the same as a normal close, with nothing lost. Filed as a follow-up for the next tools part
